incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: No federal limited partnership statute exists in Canada. The limited partnership is formed under a provincial Limited Partnership Act and thereafter recognized across Canada through interjurisdictional movement. This dossier references the Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.16, s. 2(1) and s. 9, together with the federal Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), s. 102 for partnership classification.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Business Registry, Companies and Personal Property Securities Branch, Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery; Canada Revenue Agency for federal tax registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Limited Partnership (Form 3 under the Limited Partnerships Act)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum or escrow requirement under the Limited Partnerships Act. Capital contributions are contractual and must be described in the limited partnership agreement; funds may be held in an escrow or segregated trust account pending the launch of commercial operations.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Limited Partnership accepts the general partner's capital contribution and all limited partner subscription amounts set out in the attached capital table; that the registered office is established at the address recorded in the Declaration of Limited Partnership; that the general partner appoints the initial officers with authority to open bank accounts, register for CRA program accounts, and execute Steam and PlayStation Store payee agreements; that the Declaration be filed with the Registrar; and that all governing resolutions and partnership records be maintained at the registered office. This resolution is effective immediately upon adoption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry – Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed limited partnership name and receive a name search report. Verify that the name is distinguishable from existing corporate and business names and reserve the name if required by the Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit an alternate name or file a written reconsideration request with the Registry within 30 days, providing evidence of the requested name's distinctiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute the limited partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered legal counsel or notary in Ontario
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement covering capital contributions, profit and loss allocation, management rights, transfer restrictions, governing law, and the general partner's authority. Execute the agreement by the general partner and all limited partners before proceeding to registration.
required_dossiers: Legal opinion or tax classification memorandum
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a confidentiality or regulatory defect is identified, amend the schedule and obtain fresh execution pages from each partner; the amended agreement will govern formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Declaration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Business Registry, Companies and Personal Property Securities Branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 3 Declaration of Limited Partnership, attach the executed limited partnership agreement and NUANS report, ensure the declaration is sworn or affirmed before an authorized witness, and submit the document together with the applicable filing fee.
required_dossiers: Statutory declaration of agent or authorized person
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a query or rejection, correct the specific information in the declaration, re-execute the statutory declaration, and resubmit the amended filing within 15 days of the notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register federal program accounts with the Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a federal Business Number and open the necessary program accounts including GST/HST, payroll, and possibly import/export accounts. Provide the LP registration evidence and all partners' identifying information in the CRA business registration portal.
required_dossiers: Certificate or receipt of the Declaration of Limited Partnership
Partners' legal names, dates of birth, and addresses
Evidence of the general partner's authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects or flags a registration, file an RC1 amendment or call the CRA Business Division within 21 days to reconcile the discrepancy, and provide corrected partnership documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish banking and digital store payout infrastructure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Schedule I Canadian bank plus Valve Corporation and PlayStation Store developer onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a partnership business bank account using the registered limited partnership documents and complete KYC diligence for the general partner and each limited partner. Enroll the partnership as a payout recipient with Steam Direct and PlayStation Partner to receive store proceeds in the legal entity name.
required_dossiers: Declaration of Limited Partnership registration receipt
Bank account application and KYC forms
Steam and PlayStation store onboarding forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a payout provider or bank requests additional identity information, provide certified copies of partner identification and updated ownership schedules; if non-resident ownership is challenged, provide an opinion on treaty withholding and business presence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establish corporate governance and maintenance registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt first board or general partner resolutions, maintain a registered office record, create a partner and interest register, and store the minute book at the registered office. Prepare the initial statutory declaration confirming that the general partner is validly acting and that all filings have been made.
required_dossiers: First resolution of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If records are found deficient during any regulatory or bank inspection, correct the minute book, obtain retroactive approving resolutions where permitted, and submit revised records to the governing registry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – no manufacturing or physical industrial facility exists for digital PC and console game publishing under ISIC 5820.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required for digital store publishing; a general business registration and CRA program account are sufficient.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – digital software publishing via Steam and PlayStation Store does not constitute a physical undertaking and generates no significant environmental discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to digital publishing activities. If an office is physically occupied, universal waste and e-waste disposal must comply with provincial hazardous waste regulations and ECCC's electronic product stewardship standards; no wastewater or VOC thresholds apply to serverless remote operations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: General workplace safety compliance under the Canada Labour Code Part II if a physical office is used; local fire code certification is required for any occupied commercial premises. No structural load inspection or civil defense clearance is required for a distributed digital publishing operation without a physical production facility.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada, with filing services through the 'My Business Account' portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/cra-business-portal.html); GST/HST returns and remittances are filed via GST/HST NETFILE and CRA online banking; the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administers customs Form B13A export declarations, which are relevant only to physical media exports.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (central bank); Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) as primary banking and prudential regulator; Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for AML/CTF cross-border transaction reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility on both current and capital account items under the Canadian Payments Act and the Currency Act, with no general exchange control approvals required for foreign direct investment, profit remittance, or dividend repatriation. Dividends, royalty, and trade payments may be freely transferred in any foreign currency subject to standard AML reporting thresholds (CAD 10,000 or equivalent) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. No material hurdles exist for repatriation of profits from a Canadian limited partnership to foreign non-resident partners; however, non-resident withholding tax (Part XIII) may apply to certain distributions if classified as dividends or royalties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada does not impose any statutory requirement to surrender or convert export proceeds into Canadian dollars. No mandatory timeline or conversion ratio exists for export receipts, including proceeds from digital store sales (Steam, PlayStation). Exporters must retain records for five years for tax and customs purposes and report all cross-border transfers of CAD 10,000 or more to FINTRAC. Payments received in foreign currencies may be held, converted, or hedged freely, subject to normal banking agreements.

Operational Account (multi-currency); international trade settlement capabilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Canada does not have a dedicated EMI (Electronic Money Institution) license analogous to the EU; fintechs operate as money service businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC and may be subject to the Retail Payments Activities Act (RPAA) supervision by the Bank of Canada. Cross-border digital banking platforms (e.g., Wise Platform, Payoneer, or Mercury) can be used for specific payout collection via virtual accounts, but they are not full-service commercial banks and may not meet all escrow or capital account requirements. Legal constraints include strict beneficial ownership disclosure, lack of full deposit insurance (CDIC), and limited capacity for high-volume Canadian-dollar clearing via the Large Value Transfer System (LVTS) or Real-Time Rail settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident limited partnership, most Canadian Tier 1 banks require general partner or authorized signatory to satisfy an in-person identity verification interview at a Canadian branch or through a Canadian embassy/consulate notarization. Fully remote account opening is generally not permitted for non-resident entities due to the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and OSFI’s E-13 guideline. Some banks may offer a hybrid onboarding process subject to acceptable notarized corporate documents, detailed beneficial ownership attestations, and video call verification; however, the final discretion rests with the bank’s compliance committee. For a Canadian-resident LP with a Canadian general partner, remote onboarding is possible if directors have existing Canadian banking relationships.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners with indirect ownership structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete organisational chart identifying all individuals owning ≥10% or controlling the LP; notarized partnership agreement; certificate of registration from the relevant provincial registry; LP’s undertaking to provide annual updates on any beneficial ownership changes; audited financial statements or capital contribution proof.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk source of funds from digital store revenue (Steam, PlayStation) without clear commercial contract
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed digital distribution agreements (Steamworks Publisher Agreement, PlayStation Partner Agreement); dashboard payout statements; evidence of VIES or similar tax registration (if applicable); invoice/sales reports for the prior 12 months; as well as a written explanation of the settlement currency and netting arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent or missing economic substance evidence for an LP engaged in software publishing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Employment contracts or subcontracts for Canadian developers / publishing staff; physical office lease agreement (if any); detailed description of the Canadian operational activity (game development, QA, marketing, and retail activation); materials evidencing that Canadian personnel perform day-to-day publishing decisions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large outbound payment to foreign game developer or IP owner without licence linkage
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IP licence agreement or development contract clearly denoting payment amounts and territory; withholding tax compliance proof (for payments subject to Part XIII); payment registers matching invoices to specific contract deliverables; any applicable FATCA or CRS self-certification forms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of cryptocurrency or digital asset accounts for revenue settlement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Formal anti-money-laundering review and documented rationale for digital asset use; wallet audit trail; conversion invoices from exchange counterparties; bank-approved corporate compliance manual governing digital assets; as well as any FINTRAC MSB registration if applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions from foreign non-resident partners must be wired via the SWIFT network (MT103) or via Canadian bank corresponding accounts. The remitter must include a precise purpose code, typically 'Capital contribution to a Canadian limited partnership' or 'Foreign direct investment' using the OECD balance of payments purpose code. For CAD transfers, use the CPA’s LVTS payment rails (or AFT for smaller amounts). The receiving bank may require a copy of the executed partnership agreement and a Canadian partnership tax identification number (CRA business number) to classify the credit as a capital contribution rather than taxable distribution. For FX conversion, conducting the SWIFT credit in CAD using a correspondent bank avoids additional conversion fees; alternatively, many Tier 1 banks support same-day FX via their treasury desks with spot settlement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade disbursements to Steam, PlayStation, or other gaming platforms are normally settled via regular automated clearing house (ACH) / EFT within Canada or international wire via SWIFT MT103. For Steam’s payout, Valve Corporation typically sends revenue via international wire to the publisher’s designated bank account; the publisher’s outbound disbursements to developers or licensors may be performed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 for interbank transfers. Commercial letters of credit are not commonly used for digital service payments, as there is no physical goods trade; instead, bank guarantees or documentary collections may be used when advance payment is required. For high-value recurring payments, treasury may use direct debit from the Canadian operating account under the Canadian Payments Association (CPA) rules. Any cross-border wire exceeding CAD 10,000 must be reported to FINTRAC; no exchange control approval is needed.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (deliverable) with Canadian chartered banks, under ISDA or plain-letter master agreements
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing minor / non-convertible currencies, subject to internal bank credit approval
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) and plain-vanilla cross-currency swaps for longer-term hedging of USD/CAD flows
FX options (call/put) executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with collateral support annexation
Corridor / participating forwards offered by Canadian banks for risk reversal structures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not applicable to a Canadian limited partnership; limited partnerships are generally registered and maintained under applicable provincial or territorial legislation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No federal annual return deadline; comply with the formation province or territory's annual declaration, renewal, or information filing rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No federal late fee or federal strike-off mechanism; provincial or territorial consequences may include late fees, loss of good standing, cancellation, dissolution, or administrative dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership information return, Form T5013, where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due within five months after the partnership's fiscal period-end; filing obligation depends on the Income Tax Act criteria and partnership profile
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties may apply under the Income Tax Act; additional penalties may apply for failure to provide required information or repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Provincial or territorial limited partnership annual declaration or renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate or partnership registry of the formation province or territory
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Varies by province or territory; commonly annual, based on the registration date or prescribed anniversary period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry-specific late fees, suspension or cancellation of registration, loss of good standing, and possible administrative dissolution or termination after statutory cure periods

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return, where the partnership is taxable as a corporation or has a separate filing obligation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency and, where applicable, the relevant provincial or territorial tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally six months after the corporation's tax year-end; not ordinarily applicable to a fiscally transparent Canadian limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, arrears interest, instalment interest, and potential reassessment; applicability depends on the entity's tax classification

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general Canadian federal statutory audit requirement applies to a limited partnership. An independent audit may be required by the partnership agreement, lender or investor terms, securities requirements, a regulated business activity, or applicable provincial legislation
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP, including Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises where applicable, or IFRS where elected or required; tax reporting follows Canadian federal and applicable provincial tax rules

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: A limited partnership has no federal annual beneficial-ownership confirmation filing. Maintain current records of partners, capital interests, ownership and control changes, and beneficial owners where required by applicable provincial law, tax rules, anti-money-laundering obligations, financial institutions, or the partnership agreement. Update records promptly after transfers or control changes and confirm them at least annually as an internal control
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register or record of partners and partnership interests, as required by the formation province or territory
Records of capital contributions, transfers, distributions, and changes in general or limited partner status
Minute or written-resolution book for partner and management decisions, where maintained under the partnership agreement
Beneficial-ownership and control records where required by applicable law or compliance policy

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 300-1,200 annually for registered-office, records-office, and local-agent services, excluding provincial registry fees and tax filings
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000-15,000 for an independent audit of a small private limited partnership; no audit fee is mandatory unless an audit requirement applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal small business rate for active business income (38% combined federal and provincial for larger entities)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SR&ED tax credits (refundable up to 35%), investment tax credits, accelerated capital cost allowance, manufacturing and processing profits deduction

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporate Tax Return via CRA My Business for corporations; Limited partnerships do not file T2 but partners report on T1 personal return. T1135 for foreign property if applicable
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For corporations: June 15 or 2 months after fiscal year-end if later. For LPs: No entity deadline; partners' individual returns due April 30 (or June 15 for trusts)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reporting of partnership income, losses, and deductions allocated to the partner
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must report worldwide income; withholding tax may apply to certain partnership distributions or income if structured as dividends from a Canadian corp

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties: 5% of tax payable per month (max 12 months) plus interest. For non-filing of required forms, additional penalties up to $25,000 per form

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% for non-residents on dividends from Canadian corporations (not applicable to LP distributions which are taxed as income)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Apply for reduced withholding tax under applicable DTA by submitting application to CRA with supporting documentation; TRC (Treaty Relief Certificate) issued if approved
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 10% statutory, reduced under treaties (e.g. 0-5% with US); Interest: 25% statutory, reduced under treaties (e.g. 0% with many countries)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: $250,000 CAD (threshold for value of controlled transactions requiring local file and master file documentation)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: ESR applies to non-resident entities controlled by Canadian residents; Canadian LP has full economic substance as it carries on business in Canada

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate misrepresentation of income or claiming false deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties including fines up to $1 million and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalties for gross negligence
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for willful evasion; potential criminal charges, restitution orders, and disqualification from directorship

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining LP without real business operations or employees in Canada
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under Income Tax Act for non-compliance with substance requirements; potential recharacterization of income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners may be personally liable; CRA may assess tax as if income was earned directly, plus penalties and interest

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation or apply arm's length principle to related party transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustments to income by CRA; penalties up to 10% of transaction value; interest on underpayments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for penalties if they authorized or acquiesced in non-compliance

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct proper due diligence on beneficial owners or report suspicious transactions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to $100,000 under Proceeds of Crime Act; potential criminal charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers personally liable for fines and potential imprisonment for willful non-compliance
